Name: Bulbasaur
Ecology: Bulbasaur are commonly found in grassy plains and forests, often near bodies of water. They are herbivores, primarily feeding on berries, leaves, and plant roots. These Pokémon are social creatures, living in small groups and displaying a calm and docile nature. They are known to share nutrients with the seed on their back, ensuring its healthy growth.

Name: Ivysaur
Ecology: Ivysaur typically inhabit forests and jungles, seeking areas with ample sunlight and moisture. They are primarily herbivores, consuming leaves, fruits, and occasionally nectar. Ivysaur are generally solitary Pokémon, though they may gather in small groups during mating season. They are known for their gentle nature, but can become territorial when disturbed.

Name: Venusaur
Ecology: Venusaur are found in lush forests and jungles, where they can bask in the sunlight to fuel their large flower. They are herbivores, feeding on sunlight and absorbing nutrients from the soil through their roots. Venusaur are typically solitary creatures, but they have been observed leading groups of smaller Pokémon. They are known for their protective nature and ability to calm aggressive Pokémon with the scent of their flower.

Name: Charmander
Ecology: Charmander are commonly found in warm, rocky areas, particularly near volcanoes. They are solitary creatures but sometimes gather in small groups to share warmth. Charmander primarily feed on insects and berries. They are known for their docile nature but can become aggressive if threatened.

Name: Charmeleon
Ecology: Charmeleon typically inhabit mountainous regions and rocky terrains. They are solitary Pokémon with a fierce and competitive nature. Their diet consists mainly of insects and small Pokémon. Charmeleon are known to be more aggressive than their pre-evolution, often seeking out battles to prove their strength.
